passages.title: Ahaziah seeks an oracle and Elijah answers
passages.summary: Injured Ahaziah sends messengers toward Ekron. Elijah announces his death. Two armed groups die, while the third captain pleads for life. The first two captains demand that Elijah come down. The third asks for mercy and survives.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: How does the third captain’s request differ from the first two orders?

passages.title: Elijah departs and Elisha takes up the mantle
passages.summary: Elijah and Elisha travel through Bethel and Jericho to the Jordan. Elisha receives the mantle, heals water, and encounters mocking youths. Elisha picks up Elijah’s cloak and takes up his work. His first acts show both help and judgment.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Institute manual connects the mantle with prophetic authority and distinguishes translation from resurrection.

passages.title: An alliance fights Moab
passages.summary: Joram, Jehoshaphat, and Edom’s king seek Elisha during a water crisis. They attack Moab. Mesha sacrifices his firstborn, and Israel withdraws. The alliance wins battles but withdraws after Mesha sacrifices his son. The ending raises questions about wrath.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual proposes retreat after the heir’s death. It presents the reason as possible.

passages.title: Oil, hospitality, a restored child, and food
passages.summary: A widow receives oil to pay debt. A Shunammite woman hosts Elisha, receives a son, and seeks help when he dies. Other food miracles follow. The women ask for help and act on Elisha’s words. The Shunammite refuses to leave him when her child dies.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me connects Elisha’s care and miracles with Christ’s ministry.

passages.title: Naaman accepts help and Gehazi pursues payment
passages.summary: A captive girl directs Naaman toward Israel’s prophet. Elisha sends him to wash in the Jordan. Gehazi secretly obtains gifts and receives judgment. Naaman receives help from people with less power. A captive girl and servants guide his choices.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me emphasizes humility and receiving help from people with less status.

passages.title: An axe floats, enemies receive food, and Samaria suffers
passages.summary: Elisha recovers an axe head and protects his servant at Dothan. Captured soldiers receive a meal. Later, Samaria’s siege brings famine and a desperate complaint. Elisha feeds captured enemies and sends them home. A later siege brings hunger to Samaria.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me uses the servant’s opened eyes to teach trust in unseen divine help.

passages.title: Four excluded men find an abandoned camp
passages.summary: Four men with a skin condition leave the gate and discover the Syrian camp abandoned. They bring news, and Samaria’s food prices fall. Four men find food outside the city. They decide the hungry people must hear the news.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me invites trust in the fulfillment of God’s word.

passages.title: The Shunammite returns and Hazael takes power
passages.summary: The Shunammite returns and asks for her land. Elisha meets Hazael in Damascus. The chapter also records Judah’s next kings. The Shunammite’s return shows how famine can cost a family its home. The king orders her property restored.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: What help does the Shunammite need after returning from famine?

passages.title: Jehu is anointed and kills the rulers
passages.summary: An unnamed prophetic messenger anoints Jehu. Jehu kills Joram and Ahaziah, then orders Jezebel’s death at Jezreel. Jehu uses earlier warnings to explain his killings. The change of king destroys two royal households.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual distinguishes a predicted political outcome from approval of Jehu’s methods.

passages.title: Jehu destroys households and Baal’s sanctuary
passages.summary: Jehu kills Ahab’s descendants and Ahaziah’s relatives. He traps Baal’s worshipers and kills them. Yet he keeps Jeroboam’s golden calves. Jehu ends Ahab’s royal line and Baal’s temple worship. His own worship still draws criticism.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older Church manual questions Jehu's motives.

passages.title: Joash is hidden and crowned
passages.summary: Athaliah seizes power. Jehosheba hides Joash and his nurse. Jehoiada arranges the child’s coronation, covenant renewal, and Athaliah’s execution. Jehosheba and a nurse save Joash before he becomes king. Their hidden care protects his life.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual emphasizes the child’s protection and Jehoiada’s guidance.

passages.title: Joash changes the temple repair system
passages.summary: Joash and Jehoiada direct repairs through a collection chest and workers. Joash sends treasure to Hazael, and conspirators later kill him. Temple repairs stall until the payment system changes. Trusted workers then use the money for repairs.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual studies the collection system and Jehoiada’s support.

passages.title: Northern kings and Elisha’s death
passages.summary: Jehoahaz faces Syrian pressure. His son Joash visits dying Elisha. The arrow signs precede victories, and a burial story reports restored life. Jehoahaz asks God for relief from Syria. Elisha’s last signs promise Joash victories over Syria.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual connects Elisha’s arrows with victories over Syria.

passages.title: Amaziah loses a war and Jeroboam restores territory
passages.summary: Amaziah spares his enemies’ children. He wins in Edom but loses to Israel’s Joash. Jeroboam later restores Israel’s border. Amaziah follows the law by sparing the children. His pride after victory leads to another costly war.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual studies Amaziah’s divided commitment and his failure to heed warning.

passages.title: Kings rise and fall as Assyria gains power
passages.summary: Azariah and Jotham rule Judah. Israel’s throne changes through repeated conspiracies. Menahem pays Pul, and Tiglath Pileser deports northern communities. Repeated plots bring new kings to Israel. Assyrian demands then place heavy costs on the people.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual connects Uzziah’s account in Chronicles with respect for priesthood authority.

passages.title: Ahaz seeks Assyrian help and changes the altar
passages.summary: Rezin and Pekah attack Judah. Ahaz sends treasure to Tiglath Pileser. Urijah constructs an altar based on one Ahaz sees in Damascus. Ahaz seeks Assyria’s help and copies an altar from Damascus. His alliance changes both Judah’s finances and worship.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: How does Ahaz’s need for foreign help change temple worship?

passages.title: Samaria falls and the narrator explains exile
passages.summary: Hoshea seeks Egypt’s help against Assyria. Assyria captures Samaria and removes its people. New settlers bring their own gods. The book explains Israel’s fall through broken commitments to God. It then describes the mixed worship of new settlers.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual applies the fall to the need to heed prophetic warnings.

passages.title: Hezekiah changes worship and faces Assyria
passages.summary: Hezekiah removes shrines and the bronze serpent. Sennacherib captures towns, demands payment, and sends men to threaten Jerusalem. Assyria attacks Judah and demands payment. Its spokesman tries to break the people’s trust in Hezekiah.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me studies Hezekiah’s trust during threats.

passages.title: Hezekiah prays and Isaiah answers
passages.summary: Hezekiah seeks Isaiah and prays over the threat. Isaiah announces deliverance. The army suffers a great loss, and Sennacherib later dies in his own land. Hezekiah brings the threat to God. Isaiah promises relief, and Jerusalem survives the attack.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me encourages prayer and trust when facing severe difficulties.

passages.title: Hezekiah recovers and welcomes Babylon’s envoys
passages.summary: Isaiah announces Hezekiah’s recovery and a sign. Hezekiah shows his treasures to Babylonian visitors. Isaiah warns that later generations will face exile. Hezekiah recovers and receives visitors from Babylon. Showing them his treasures leads to Isaiah’s warning.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual connects Hezekiah’s prayer with trust in divine care.

passages.title: Manasseh and Amon restore forbidden worship
passages.summary: Manasseh restores shrines, practices forbidden rites, and sheds innocent blood. Amon continues his father’s ways and is killed by servants. Josiah succeeds. Manasseh restores worship that Hezekiah removed. Unlike Chronicles, Kings gives no account of his repentance.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: Manasseh reverses many of Hezekiah's changes. How do a leader's choices affect other people?

passages.title: The law scroll is found and Huldah responds
passages.summary: Hilkiah finds the law scroll during temple work. Shaphan reads it to Josiah. A delegation seeks Huldah, who announces judgment and mercy toward Josiah. The king's men seek Huldah's answer about the book. Her warning leads Josiah to change worship.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me connects scripture with changes of heart and commitment.

passages.title: Josiah renews the covenant and removes shrines
passages.summary: Josiah reads the covenant, removes worship objects and shrines, and celebrates Passover. He dies at Megiddo. Jehoahaz is deposed, and Jehoiakim rules. Josiah removes worship objects and renews Passover. Judah's later kings return to the practices he opposed.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me uses Josiah’s covenant to teach wholehearted commitment.

passages.title: Babylon takes treasure and deports Jehoiachin
passages.summary: Jehoiakim rebels against Babylon. Jehoiachin surrenders Jerusalem and is deported with his household and other residents. Nebuchadnezzar appoints Zedekiah. Babylon removes the king, workers, soldiers, and many families. The city loses people as well as treasures.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual connects Zedekiah’s setting with Lehi in the Book of Mormon. This is an LDS cross-reference.

passages.title: Jerusalem is destroyed and a prisoner receives favor
passages.summary: Jerusalem falls. Zedekiah is captured, the temple burns, and captives are taken away. Gedaliah is killed. Jehoiachin later receives favor in Babylon. Babylon destroys the temple and takes people away. Later kindness gives the captive king some relief.
passages.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: What changes when Jehoiachin receives kindness at the end of the book?

lds.text: Come, Follow Me encourages prayer and trust when facing severe difficulties.

events.title: Hezekiah recovers and welcomes Babylon’s envoys
events.summary: Isaiah announces Hezekiah’s recovery and a sign. Hezekiah shows his treasures to Babylonian visitors. Isaiah warns that later generations will face exile.
events.detail: Hezekiah recovers and receives visitors from Babylon. Showing them his treasures leads to Isaiah’s warning.
events.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual connects Hezekiah’s prayer with trust in divine care.

events.title: Manasseh and Amon restore forbidden worship
events.summary: Manasseh restores shrines, practices forbidden rites, and sheds innocent blood. Amon continues his father’s ways and is killed by servants. Josiah succeeds.
events.detail: Manasseh restores worship that Hezekiah removed. Unlike Chronicles, Kings gives no account of his repentance.
events.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: Manasseh reverses many of Hezekiah's changes. How do a leader's choices affect other people?

events.title: The law scroll is found and Huldah responds
events.summary: Hilkiah finds the law scroll during temple work. Shaphan reads it to Josiah. A delegation seeks Huldah, who announces judgment and mercy toward Josiah.
events.detail: The king's men seek Huldah's answer about the book. Her warning leads Josiah to change worship.
events.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me connects scripture with changes of heart and commitment.

events.title: Josiah renews the covenant and removes shrines
events.summary: Josiah reads the covenant, removes worship objects and shrines, and celebrates Passover. He dies at Megiddo. Jehoahaz is deposed, and Jehoiakim rules.
events.detail: Josiah removes worship objects and renews Passover. Judah's later kings return to the practices he opposed.
events.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: Come, Follow Me uses Josiah’s covenant to teach wholehearted commitment.

events.title: Babylon takes treasure and deports Jehoiachin
events.summary: Jehoiakim rebels against Babylon. Jehoiachin surrenders Jerusalem and is deported with his household and other residents. Nebuchadnezzar appoints Zedekiah.
events.detail: Babylon removes the king, workers, soldiers, and many families. The city loses people as well as treasures.
events.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

lds.text: The older manual connects Zedekiah’s setting with Lehi in the Book of Mormon. This is an LDS cross-reference.

events.title: Jerusalem is destroyed and a prisoner receives favor
events.summary: Jerusalem falls. Zedekiah is captured, the temple burns, and captives are taken away. Gedaliah is killed. Jehoiachin later receives favor in Babylon.
events.detail: Babylon destroys the temple and takes people away. Later kindness gives the captive king some relief.
events.uncertainty: Named towns and approximate reference regions. Exact buildings, camps, and disputed sites remain uncertain.

guides.title: Study 2 Kings
guides.description: Follow selected chapters through the book.

steps.title: Ahaziah seeks an oracle and Elijah answers
steps.text: Injured Ahaziah sends messengers toward Ekron. Elijah announces his death. Two armed groups die, while the third captain pleads for life. The first two captains demand that Elijah come down. The third asks for mercy and survives.

steps.title: Northern kings and Elisha’s death
steps.text: Jehoahaz faces Syrian pressure. His son Joash visits dying Elisha. The arrow signs precede victories, and a burial story reports restored life. Jehoahaz asks God for relief from Syria. Elisha’s last signs promise Joash victories over Syria.

steps.title: Jerusalem is destroyed and a prisoner receives favor
steps.text: Jerusalem falls. Zedekiah is captured, the temple burns, and captives are taken away. Gedaliah is killed. Jehoiachin later receives favor in Babylon. Babylon destroys the temple and takes people away. Later kindness gives the captive king some relief.

textRoutes.summary: Rezin and Pekah attack Judah. Ahaz sends treasure to Tiglath Pileser. Urijah constructs an altar based on one Ahaz sees in Damascus.
textRoutes.detail: Ahaz seeks Assyria’s help and copies an altar from Damascus. His alliance changes both Judah’s finances and worship.

textRoutes.title: Hezekiah prays and Isaiah answers
textRoutes.summary: Hezekiah seeks Isaiah and prays over the threat. Isaiah announces deliverance. The army suffers a great loss, and Sennacherib later dies in his own land.
textRoutes.detail: Hezekiah brings the threat to God. Isaiah promises relief, and Jerusalem survives the attack.

textRoutes.title: Babylon takes treasure and deports Jehoiachin
textRoutes.summary: Jehoiakim rebels against Babylon. Jehoiachin surrenders Jerusalem and is deported with his household and other residents. Nebuchadnezzar appoints Zedekiah.
textRoutes.detail: Babylon removes the king, workers, soldiers, and many families. The city loses people as well as treasures.

textRoutes.title: Jerusalem is destroyed and a prisoner receives favor
textRoutes.summary: Jerusalem falls. Zedekiah is captured, the temple burns, and captives are taken away. Gedaliah is killed. Jehoiachin later receives favor in Babylon.
textRoutes.detail: Babylon destroys the temple and takes people away. Later kindness gives the captive king some relief.
